claims.text: Redis is a server that runs as its own process and keeps values under keys in memory; every client connected to it reads and writes the same keys.
claims.source_hint: Redis docs: Get started / What is Redis (in-memory data store, client-server)

claims.text: A key-value store only stores a value under a key and returns it by that key; used this way it has no tables and no JOIN.
claims.source_hint: glossary entry key-value-store; Redis docs: Keys and values / Strings

claims.text: docker-compose.yml @ stage-2 defines service redis: image redis:8.10.2-alpine, container_name donhang-redis, hostname redis, on network donhang (172.28.0.15), no ports: section; db publishes 5432:5432.

Containers on the same Compose network reach a service by its service name, so the api reaches redis as redis just as it reaches db as db. The redis service publishes no port, so no program on your machine reaches it at localhost:6379; the api and the lab box reach it over the donhang network.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: Networking in Compose (service name lookup); Compose file reference: ports

claims.text: The api's ConnectionStrings__Redis setting starts with redis:6379 (full value "redis:6379,abortConnect=false"): the host name, then the port the Redis server listens on (6379, the default).
SET key value EX seconds stores the value and sets the key's expiry to that many seconds.
TTL key returns the remaining time to live in seconds; it returns -2 when the key does not exist.
When a key's time to live runs out, Redis deletes it by itself; a GET afterwards finds no value.
claims.source_hint: Redis docs: commands/expire (keys with a timeout are automatically deleted); commands/get (nil when key does not exist)

claims.text: SET on a key that already holds a value overwrites the value, and any previous time to live on the key is discarded (here replaced by EX 2).
claims.source_hint: Redis docs: commands/set ('Any previous time to live associated with the key is discarded on successful SET')

claims.text: Redis string values are stored as given (binary-safe); Redis does not parse or validate the JSON text, so SET of a value with "priceVnd":-5 answers OK.
claims.source_hint: Redis docs: Strings data type (binary-safe, any kind of data)

claims.text: Redis keeps its data in memory, which is what makes its reads fast.
claims.source_hint: Redis docs: introduction (in-memory data structure store)

claims.text: Đơn Hàng stores every fact in PostgreSQL and treats anything in Redis as a copy that can be rebuilt from it (compose comment on the redis service; STAGE.md).

redis-basics.sh re-runs itself in the lab box via lab-run.sh when not in a container (line 5); redis() echoes 'redis> <args>' then runs redis-cli -h redis; it SETs product:3 EX 60, GET, TTL, then SET EX 2, sleep 3, TTL, GET.
Captured output: first TTL answers 60; after the EX 2 set and 3 s sleep, TTL answers -2 and GET prints an empty line.

redis-cli -h <host> connects to the Redis server at that host name; the lab box (container donhang-lab on the donhang network, where redis-basics.sh runs) installs the Alpine redis package for redis-cli.
claims.source_hint: Redis docs: redis-cli (-h hostname); examples/don-hang @ stage-2: lab/Dockerfile:2,10

claims.text: deploy/k8s/api.yaml @ stage-2 runs the api with replicas: 2, two copies side by side.
A Dictionary lives in the memory of one process: each API process has its own, and a restart of the process empties it.
docker compose restart api restarts only the api service's container; the redis container and its keys are not touched.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: docker compose restart (restarts the named services)

claims.text: products has a primary key and CHECK (price_vnd > 0); order_items.product_id REFERENCES products (id).
Keeping the facts in PostgreSQL, where its constraints hold, and only copies in Redis is the right split for Đơn Hàng's products, because Redis as used here enforces no rule on the values.
